findings.title: Copy-paste null-check validates grantType twice, never validates rawTokenId
findings.body: In services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/AccessTokenContext.java line 73 the constructor does Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") instead of checking rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is therefore accepted and later used in encodeTokenId as ':' + null, producing a corrupt token id ("...:null") or NPEs downstream, while the duplicate grantType check adds no value.

findings.title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks all existing custom grant factories
findings.body: In server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java the new method String getShortcut() is abstract with no default. Any third-party OAuth2GrantTypeFactory compiled against the old interface will fail at runtime with AbstractMethodError/NoSuchMethodError when DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory casts to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory and calls getShortcut(), breaking server startup/token issuance. It should be a default method returning "na"/null.

findings.title: Context constructor dereferences formParams without null check
findings.body: In server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java line 102 the constructor does this.grantType = formParams.getFirst(...). If formParams is null the token endpoint fails with NullPointerException. The old constructor never touched formParams, so this is a new crash path for any caller constructing a Context with null/delayed form params.

findings.title: Removal of Context(Context) copy constructor breaks API compatibility
findings.body: In server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java the public copy constructor Context(Context context) was deleted. External grant implementations or extensions that copied the context will no longer compile/link. Removal is unnecessary for adding the grantType field and should be restored or deprecated.

findings.title: No null handling for missing user/client session causes token issuance NPE
findings.body: In services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java line 47 getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext unconditionally does clientSessionContext.getClientSession().getUserSession() and then userSession.getPersistenceState()/isOffline(). For service-account, token-exchange transient, or any flow with no user session this throws NullPointerException inside TokenManager.initToken, turning all access-token creation into a 500 error. It should map missing session to UNKNOWN.

findings.title: Unknown grant type makes access-token creation throw instead of falling back
findings.body: In services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java lines 109-111 encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException when factory.getShortcutByGrantType returns null. TokenManager.initToken calls this unconditionally for every access token, so any token with a grant id that is not a registered OAuth2GrantType (custom grants, implicit/hybrid, admin API, SAML exchanges) fails issuance with 500. Missing grant already falls back to "na"; unknown grants should do the same.

findings.title: Malformed token IDs throw instead of returning UNKNOWN context
findings.body: In services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java lines 74-93 getTokenContextFromTokenId throws IllegalArgumentException when the prefix before ':' is not exactly 6 chars or shortcuts are unknown. Token IDs are untrusted input presented on introspection/userinfo/resource endpoints; throwing forces every future caller to catch or it becomes a 500 instead of invalid_token handling. No-colon legacy IDs correctly return UNKNOWN, malformed colon IDs should do the same.

findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher inverted and checks wrong substring
findings.body: In testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java line 483 isAccessTokenId does if (items[0].substring(3,5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false; This is backwards (returns false on match) and slices the wrong characters: for a 6-char prefix like "onrtac" the grant occupies substring(4,6), not (3,5). The result is correct tokens fail the assertion and wrong-grant tokens can pass, plus short prefixes throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of returning false.
